summary: Mount Walker lookout (1931-1967) in Olympic NF; WWII Aircraft Warning Service station; site is now a Forest Service viewpoint reached by road in summer.

facts.design: Gable-roofed L-4 cab on a ground house; the Forest Lookouts page calls the ground house a standard R-6 plan, 14 by 14 feet, wood frame
facts.status_note: Cab removed or destroyed in 1967 (sources differ on the wording); the summit is now a Forest Service viewpoint

staffing.status: Air Warning Service station in 1942; manned as a fire lookout per a May 1956 news item; no later staffing described

access.note: Forest Service viewpoint site with north and south viewpoints, parking and vault toilets; road gated in winter

visit.trail_note: Drive up the gravel road in summer; in winter park at the gate and walk the road or the trail, about 2 miles to the first viewpoint and half a mile further to the south viewpoint

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Sites record says the cab was removed in 1967; firelookout.com and Willhite's page say it was destroyed that year. All say it was gone by 1967.
The Sites record and Willhite describe a gable-roofed L-4 cab; the Forest Lookouts page calls the ground house a standard R-6 plan. The brief's R-6 is kept, with the L-4 cab noted.
The Forest Lookouts page quotes an inventory dating a 12-by-18 garage to 1940, and an AWS report saying the AWS added a 12-by-18 garage. The sources do not say whether these are the same building.

Willhite's viewpoint page gives a summit elevation of 2,085 feet. The brief's 854.7 m is about 2,804 feet, which Willhite's figure does not match. The brief value is kept; Willhite's figure is not used.

notes_for_editor: Access: the Forest Service viewpoint page includes an alert about weekday closures on NF-2870; check current road status before anyone plans a visit. The brief's access 'unknown' is replaced by public. The brief's elevation (854.7 m) is kept; Willhite's 2,085 ft figure is treated as an error. The firelookout.com photos are credited to the Fire Lookout Museum and National Archives; none was added because no image URLs appeared in the fetched text.
